title: Kozma's centrally excited walk converges to a Euclidean ball
summary: A centrally excited random walk on ${\mathbb Z}^d$ moves like simple random walk, except that its first step from each site has a drift of fixed size toward the origin. Kozma (2007) conjectured that after $n$ steps the visited set approximates a ball with radius of order $n^{ 1/(d+1)}$. We prove this in every dimension $d\geq2$ and show that the rescaled numbers of visits converge uniformly to a cone, which is the potential generated by the drift on a ball.
